parts:
Hi all,

I am having an issue renaming my photos with imageRename. I have exiftool downloaded and it is functioning fine, however, when I try to run the code to rename my photos I keep getting error messages. I will link photos of the code and the error messages below.

It could be with noting I have had a colleague run the same code with the same images on his windows computer without issue (I am on a Mac). 

I am new to this so any suggestions would go a long way!

Cheers, 
Benjamin

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Problem with remaining photos to metadata info
parts:
Hi Benjamin,

wow, looks like you scored all error messages at once. I have no experience with Mac myself, so if other users know more, please feel free to contribute. It may have to do with some hidden directories on Mac which R reads out. Since it runs on Windows it is most likely something Mac-related.

It looks like the function considers your folders "camera1", "camera2" etc. as stations. Is that correct so far?

but then somehow there is a "station" NA. I don't know how that happens, but it's clearly wrong.

Can you please share the output of:

dirs_short <- list.dirs(wd_images_raw, full.names = FALSE,  recursive = FALSE)

dirs_short

And then:

list.files(dirs_short[1], , recursive = TRUE)

That might give some indication as to what goes wrong here.

Best,

Jürgen

Thanks for getting back to me. Correct, "camera1", "camera2" etc. are both stations and only contain one camera. 

I am not sure how there is a station NA either? Some of the folders (i.e., "camera1") have no photos due to camera failure but it there are no extra unnamed files that would show up as NA. There also appears to be a file not found that just has no name and looks like three empty spaces which confuses me too. 

When running your code above I get back the following: 

Does this just mean that it is not reading any files in wd_images_raw? 

If the best course of action would be to retry on a windows computer I can try to give that a shot too.

Thanks,

Benjamin
